---
title: "Frame Conventions"
---

PX4 and ROS 2 use different coordinate frames. Every quantity exchanged over
uXRCE-DDS must be converted at the boundary. This page defines the frames,
the conversion rules, and the C++ implementations used in `uav_control`.

---

## Frame definitions

| Frame | Name | X | Y | Z | Used by |
|-------|------|---|---|---|---------|
| World inertial | **NED** | North | East | Down | PX4 internally, `VehicleLocalPosition`, `VehicleOdometry` |
| Body | **FRD** | Forward | Right | Down | PX4 body-frame quantities (`VehicleAngularVelocity`, torque/thrust setpoints) |
| World inertial | **ENU** | East | North | Up | ROS 2 convention, RViz, nav_msgs |
| Body | **FLU** | Forward | Left | Up | ROS 2 `geometry_msgs`, most controllers |

::: {.callout-note}
PX4 `VehicleOdometry` reports position in NED and velocity in FRD. Angular
velocity (`VehicleAngularVelocity`) is in FRD. Attitude quaternion
(`VehicleAttitude`) expresses the rotation from FRD to NED.
:::

---

## Vector conversions

### NED <-> ENU

The axes permute as: $x_\text{ENU} = y_\text{NED}$, $y_\text{ENU} = x_\text{NED}$, $z_\text{ENU} = -z_\text{NED}$.

The same relation holds in reverse (the transform is its own inverse):

$$
\begin{pmatrix} x \\ y \\ z \end{pmatrix}_\text{NED}
= \begin{pmatrix} y \\ x \\ -z \end{pmatrix}_\text{ENU}
$$

```cpp
inline Eigen::Vector3d ned_to_enu(const Eigen::Vector3d& v) {
    return {v.y(), v.x(), -v.z()};
}
// enu_to_ned is identical (the mapping is its own inverse)
```

### FRD <-> FLU

Only the lateral and vertical axes flip: $y_\text{FLU} = -y_\text{FRD}$, $z_\text{FLU} = -z_\text{FRD}$.

$$
\begin{pmatrix} x \\ y \\ z \end{pmatrix}_\text{FLU}
= \begin{pmatrix} x \\ -y \\ -z \end{pmatrix}_\text{FRD}
$$

```cpp
inline Eigen::Vector3d frd_to_flu(const Eigen::Vector3d& v) {
    return {v.x(), -v.y(), -v.z()};
}
// flu_to_frd is identical
```

---

## Quaternion conversion (ENU/FLU <-> NED/FRD)

Converting a quaternion requires two rotations applied in sequence:

1. **NED_ENU_Q** — rotates the world frame: $R_z(\pi/2) \cdot R_x(\pi)$
2. **AIRCRAFT_BASELINK_Q** — rotates the body frame: $R_x(\pi)$

```cpp
inline Eigen::Quaterniond enu_flu_to_ned_frd(const Eigen::Quaterniond& q) {
    // World-frame rotation: 90 deg yaw + 180 deg roll (ENU <-> NED)
    const Eigen::Quaterniond NED_ENU_Q =
        Eigen::AngleAxisd(M_PI_2, Eigen::Vector3d::UnitZ()) *
        Eigen::AngleAxisd(M_PI,   Eigen::Vector3d::UnitX());

    // Body-frame rotation: 180 deg roll (FLU <-> FRD)
    const Eigen::Quaterniond AIRCRAFT_BASELINK_Q =
        Eigen::AngleAxisd(M_PI, Eigen::Vector3d::UnitX());

    return (NED_ENU_Q * q) * AIRCRAFT_BASELINK_Q;
}
// ned_frd_to_enu_flu: same function (the combined rotation is its own inverse)
```

::: {.callout-warning}
`VehicleAttitude.q` is stored as Hamilton `[w, x, y, z]` — not `[x, y, z, w]`.
Match the Eigen constructor argument order accordingly:
`Eigen::Quaterniond q(msg->q[0], msg->q[1], msg->q[2], msg->q[3])`.
:::

---

## Parsing `VehicleOdometry`

`VehicleOdometry` delivers all quantities in PX4 frames. Convert everything to
ENU/FLU before passing to a ROS-convention controller:

```cpp
void parse_odometry(
    const px4_msgs::msg::VehicleOdometry& msg,
    Eigen::Vector3d& pos_enu,
    Eigen::Quaterniond& att_enu_flu,
    Eigen::Vector3d& vel_enu,
    Eigen::Vector3d& omega_flu)
{
    // position: NED -> ENU
    pos_enu = ned_to_enu({msg.position[0], msg.position[1], msg.position[2]});

    // attitude: NED/FRD -> ENU/FLU
    Eigen::Quaterniond q_ned_frd(msg.q[0], msg.q[1], msg.q[2], msg.q[3]);
    att_enu_flu = ned_frd_to_enu_flu(q_ned_frd);

    // velocity: NED -> ENU
    vel_enu = ned_to_enu({msg.velocity[0], msg.velocity[1], msg.velocity[2]});

    // angular velocity: FRD -> FLU
    omega_flu = frd_to_flu({msg.angular_velocity[0],
                            msg.angular_velocity[1],
                            msg.angular_velocity[2]});
}
```

Note: `VehicleAngularVelocity` (from `/fmu/out/vehicle_angular_velocity`) also
delivers in FRD — apply `frd_to_flu` the same way.

---

## Publishing setpoints (controller -> PX4)

Setpoints go in the opposite direction: convert from controller ENU/FLU to
PX4 NED/FRD before publishing.

### Thrust (scalar)

Thrust is a scalar magnitude in the controller. PX4 expects it as a
**negative** `z` component in the body-NED frame (down is positive):

```cpp
thrust_msg.xyz[2] = -collective_thrust;   // always negative
```

### Torque vector

```cpp
Eigen::Vector3d tau_frd = flu_to_frd(tau_flu);
torque_msg.xyz[0] = tau_frd.x();
torque_msg.xyz[1] = tau_frd.y();
torque_msg.xyz[2] = tau_frd.z();
```

### Attitude quaternion

```cpp
Eigen::Quaterniond q_ned_frd = enu_flu_to_ned_frd(q_desired);
att_msg.q_d[0] = q_ned_frd.w();
att_msg.q_d[1] = q_ned_frd.x();
att_msg.q_d[2] = q_ned_frd.y();
att_msg.q_d[3] = q_ned_frd.z();
```

### Trajectory setpoint (position/velocity, NED)

`TrajectorySetpoint` positions and velocities are in NED:

```cpp
traj_msg.position = {pos_ned.x(), pos_ned.y(), pos_ned.z()};
traj_msg.velocity = {vel_ned.x(), vel_ned.y(), vel_ned.z()};
traj_msg.yaw = yaw_ned;   // measured CW from North
```

Convert from ENU before filling: `pos_ned = enu_to_ned(pos_enu)`.

---

## Altitude sign

In NED, altitude increases **downward** (z is positive down). A drone hovering
2 m above the ground has $z \approx -2$. This affects trajectory setpoints,
height checks, and obstacle bounds:

```cpp
// NED: negative z = above ground
constexpr float TAKEOFF_ALT_NED = -5.0f;   // 5 m above ground

// ENU (RViz / nav_msgs): positive z = above ground
constexpr float TAKEOFF_ALT_ENU =  5.0f;
```

---

## Yaw convention

PX4 yaw is measured **clockwise from North** (NED convention). ROS yaw is
measured **counter-clockwise from East** (ENU convention). To extract yaw from
a quaternion in the appropriate frame:

```cpp
// From NED quaternion [w, x, y, z]
float yaw_ned = std::atan2(
    2.0f * (qw * qz + qx * qy),
    1.0f - 2.0f * (qy * qy + qz * qz));
```

---

## Quick reference

| Quantity | PX4 frame | Controller frame | Conversion |
|----------|-----------|-----------------|------------|
| Position | NED | ENU | swap x/y, negate z |
| Velocity (world) | NED | ENU | swap x/y, negate z |
| Angular velocity | FRD | FLU | negate y and z |
| Attitude quaternion | NED/FRD | ENU/FLU | `enu_flu_to_ned_frd` |
| Thrust (body z) | NED (negative) | positive scalar | negate |
| Torque | FRD | FLU | negate y and z |
| Yaw | CW from North | CCW from East | negate |
